title: Lesson 15 · Adverbs to Interjections in Depth
blurb: The five classes of adverbs, comparing adverbs, classes of conjunctions, interjections, and common errors.

items.prompt:
Which class of adverb is this?

“now”

Which class of adverb is this?

“here”

Which class of adverb is this?

“why”

Which class of adverb is this?

“slowly”

Which class of adverb is this?

“very”
items.explain: “very” answers “how much?” — an adverb of degree.

items.prompt:
Which class of adverb is this?

“soon”

Which class of adverb is this?

“there”

Which class of adverb is this?

“almost”
items.explain: “almost” answers “how much?” — an adverb of degree.

items.prompt:
Which gives the correct comparative and superlative?

“fast”

Which gives the correct comparative and superlative?

“soon”

Which gives the correct comparative and superlative?

“wisely”
items.explain: An -ly adverb — use more, most: more wisely, most wisely.

items.prompt:
Which gives the correct comparative and superlative?

“well”

Which gives the correct comparative and superlative?

“slowly”
items.explain: An -ly adverb — use more, most: more slowly, most slowly.

items.prompt:
Which gives the correct comparative and superlative?

“badly”

Which kind of conjunction is this?

“and”

Which kind of conjunction is this?

“because”
items.explain: “because” joins unequal parts (a clause to a main clause) — subordinate.

items.prompt:
Which kind of conjunction is this?

“either…or”

Which kind of conjunction is this?

“but”

Which kind of conjunction is this?

“if”
items.explain: “if” joins unequal parts (a clause to a main clause) — subordinate.

items.prompt:
Which kind of conjunction is this?

“neither…nor”

Which kind of conjunction is this?

“or”

Which kind of conjunction is this?

“although”

Choose the correct word(s):

“She ___ coming.”

Choose the correct word(s):

“I ___ won.”

Choose the correct word(s):

“The scissors ___ dull.”
items.explain: “scissors” takes a plural verb: the scissors are dull.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word(s):

“Henry and Charles ___ glad.”
items.explain: Two subjects joined by “and” take a plural verb: were.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word(s):

“He ___ know the answer.”
items.explain: A singular subject takes “doesn’t”: he doesn’t know.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word(s):

“They ___ tired.”
items.explain: A plural subject takes a plural verb: they were.

items.prompt:
Which word is the interjection (the exclaiming word)?

“Ah! What a view.”
items.explain: “Ah” bursts out with feeling — the interjection.

items.prompt:
Which word is the interjection (the exclaiming word)?

“Ouch! I fell.”
items.explain: “Ouch” bursts out with feeling — the interjection.

items.prompt:
Which word is the interjection (the exclaiming word)?

“Alas, he failed.”
items.explain: “Alas” bursts out with feeling — the interjection.

items.prompt:
Which word is the interjection (the exclaiming word)?

“Hurrah, we won!”
items.explain: “Hurrah” bursts out with feeling — the interjection.

items.prompt:

“I haven’t got ___ money.”
items.explain: Avoid two negatives: haven’t got any money.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word(s):

“He ___ fast.”
items.explain: A singular subject takes a singular verb: he runs.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct word(s):

“The news ___ good.”
items.explain: “news” takes a singular verb: the news is good.
